generation.explanation: In Euclidean geometry, draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side. The other two angles match the angles formed at that line by the triangle’s sides (alternate interior angles), and those three angles make a straight angle of 180°. This depends on Euclidean parallel lines; on curved surfaces, a triangle’s angle sum can differ.
